text: Grigol Gegelia - Summoning Pawel Herczynski to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs is yet another clear proof that this government serves anti-Georgian goals and aspirations (27.04.2026, 12:12)

The summoning of Herchynski is yet another clear proof that this government always serves anti-Georgian goals and aspirations," said Grigol Gegelia, Foreign Secretary of "Lelo - Strong Georgia," regarding the summoning of EU Ambassador Pawel Herchynski.

According to Gegelia, at a time when the ambassadors of Iran and Hungary have not been summoned by the Foreign Ministry, summoning representatives of Georgia’s strategic partners shows that the “Georgian Dream” government is serving to damage the country’s strategic interests.

“At a time when the Iranian ambassador has not been summoned and questioned about why he was threatening the Georgian people in such language, at a time when the Hungarian ambassador has not been summoned and asked about a Russian spy who worked in Georgia for 4 years, what exactly we were dealing with, whether Hungary was informed, and how we should understand the fact that, under the cover of Hungarian diplomatic protection, a Russian spy was likely operating in this city, Bochorishvili now allows herself to attack all those ambassadors who represent states that are strategic partners of this country. Whether because of a statement made about Ilia State University or because of elementary pro-democratic statements, she summons for clarification the ambassadors of those states that are our country’s most important strategic partners. This clearly confirms that the so-called government is an anti-Georgian government, which is doing everything to damage our country’s national domestic and foreign policy interests,” said Grigol Gegelia.

Let me remind you that the EU Ambassador to Georgia, Pawel Herczyński, speaking in Brussels at the European External Action Service, where the documentary photo exhibition “Georgia in Focus” was opened, noted that Georgia is no longer on the right trajectory. According to the ambassador, “the government has chosen an alternative model of authoritarianism and is moving Georgia away from the European Union.”

“Georgia stands at a crossroads. Georgia’s future has not yet been written, but what is decided in the coming weeks and months will determine whether Georgia belongs to the family of European countries based on democracy, the rule of law, and human rights, or whether, unfortunately, it returns to its dark past. My main message to the Georgian people is: ‘Do not lose hope.’ We must not allow Georgia and the wonderful, warm, hospitable Georgian people to return to the dark times of violence, civil war, poverty, hardship, and corruption. This is not the future they deserve. As soon as the government expresses a desire to cooperate with us, we will do everything possible to help Georgia become a member of the European Union,” Herczyński said, as quoted by Netgazeti.
Following this statement, the ambassador was summoned to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
